title: Kuwait approves award of oilfield water separation deal

contentHtml:
KUWAIT - JANUARY 15: Oil rig workers work on the ChevronTexaco drilling platform January 15, 2003 near the Saudi Arabian border, Kuwait. Kuwait produces 10% of the worlds oil and has promised to increase production as needed in the event of a war in Iraq. (Photo by Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

Project costs $385mln

N Saeed ,  ZAWYA Projects

Kuwait has approved the award of a new contract for the separation of water at a key oilfield as part of a long-term strategy to expand its crude output capacity.

The Supreme Purchasing Committee for Kuwait Petroleum Corporation (KPC) agreed on a request by the Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) to award the project for the water separation facility in the Northern Rawdatain field at Gathering Centre 25 (GC 25) and the pumping facility at GC 30.

The contract has an estimated value of 117 million Kuwaiti dinars ($285 million), the Arab language daily Al Rai said, citing informed sources.

KOC’s request came after the winning company submitted the lowest bid that met the required conditions, provided that the awarding procedures are completed through the Central Agency for Public Tenders, the report said without identifying the winning firm.

(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
